articles.title: Honda SENSING RIDE Motorcycle Safety System (Nov 2026)
articles.excerpt: Honda introduced SENSING RIDE at EICMA 2026 on 3 November: radar at both ends of the motorcycle and 10 functions, first on the 2027 CRF1150L Africa Twin Adventure Sports.
blocks: Honda introduced "Honda SENSING RIDE", a safety and rider-assistance system for motorcycles, on 3 November 2026 at the EICMA motorcycle show in Milan. Honda says the first model to get it is the 2027 CRF1150L Africa Twin Adventure Sports, and that it plans to add the system to more models. The system uses two millimeter-wave radar units, one at each end of the motorcycle, and offers 10 functions. This article is based on Honda's own announcement and is correct as of 4 November 2026.

Honda says SENSING RIDE builds on Honda SENSING, the driver-assistance package the company offers on cars, with functions added that suit motorcycles. According to Honda, the system looks at the situation of the rider and the motorcycle and then gives notifications, warnings and operational assistance, including help with avoiding a collision.

Honda also says the system works together with its Dual Clutch Transmission (DCT), an automatic gearbox that removes the need to operate a clutch by hand. Honda states that DCT was first used on motorcycles in 2010.
How radar-based rider aids work in general

Honda's pages do not describe how the radar is used, so this section gives general background from a reference article on adaptive cruise control in cars. Radar measures distance by timing radio waves that bounce back from an object, and it can also tell how fast the gap is changing. Car systems commonly use radar at 24 GHz or 77 GHz. The same reference says that most adaptive cruise control systems count as Level 1 on the SAE scale of driving automation, which means the system helps with one task, such as speed, while the driver does everything else.

The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) in the United States makes the same point about cars: the driver still steers and must be ready to act if the system does not respond well. It also says that some drivers overestimate what such systems can do. These comments are about car systems and not about Honda's motorcycle system, but they match the warning Honda itself gives.

Adaptive Cruise Control: keeps a set speed and following distance
Adaptive Cruise Control with Stop and Go: reduces throttle and brake inputs in slow, stop-start traffic
Group Ride Assist: helps riders keep suitable spacing in a group, including a staggered formation
Distance Assist: adjusts following distance when the rider opens the throttle while approaching a vehicle ahead
Emergency Brake Assist: adds braking help when the rider brakes and a collision is likely
Forward Collision Warning: shows an alert on the meter when a collision ahead is possible
Brake Pulse: works with the forward warning to make the rider more aware
Blind Spot Information: lights a signal at the mirror when a vehicle is diagonally behind
Rear Collision Warning: flashes the indicators to warn traffic behind
Rear Distance Information: shows a display on the meter when a vehicle approaches from behind

Honda's European press release describes the 2027 model year Africa Twin family as having more power, more technology and more choice for riders, and says SENSING RIDE debuts on the Adventure Sports version. The Africa Twin range and the CBR1000RR-R Fireblade were Honda's two headline motorcycle premieres at the show, which runs at Fiera Milano from 3 to 8 November 2026, with public days from 5 to 8 November.

In the announcement Honda repeats a company target: to cut the number of traffic fatalities involving its motorcycles and cars, per 10,000 units sold, by 50 percent by 2030 compared with 2020, and to reach zero by 2050.

Honda says each function has limits and may not work as intended depending on road, weather and vehicle conditions. It asks riders to stay alert to their surroundings, and its release says riders should not overestimate what each function can do. Like the assistance systems on cars, these features are described as aids to the rider and not as a replacement for the rider's attention.

Price of the Africa Twin Adventure Sports with the system
On-sale dates and the countries where it will be sold, including India
Which other Honda models will follow
Technical details of the radar units, which Honda's page does not give
Honda's pages reviewed for this article gave no price, no on-sale date and no India plans. Check Honda's own announcements for those details when they appear.

articles.title: Honda RN0 Electric Mountain Bike Unveiled (Nov 2026)
articles.excerpt: Honda unveiled the RN0, its first high-end electric-assist mountain bike, at EICMA 2026: about 24 kg, a Shimano motor with 100 Nm and a 720 Wh battery. Price and sale dates are not given.
blocks: Honda showed the RN0, its first high-end electric-assist mountain bike, in a world premiere at EICMA 2026 in Milan on 3 November 2026. Honda says it developed the bike with ROTWILD, a German maker of electric mountain bikes. The company lists a weight of about 24 kg, a Shimano drive unit with 100 Nm of torque and 750 W peak output, and a 720 Wh battery. Honda's pages do not give a price or a sale date. Details are as of 4 November 2026.

Frame: proprietary carbon monocoque frame with a "gull-arm" swingarm, in sizes S, M and L
Weight: about 24 kg
Motor: new Shimano drive unit weighing 2.3 kg, 100 Nm maximum torque, 750 W maximum output
Battery: 720 Wh
Front suspension: FOX 36 FLOAT Factory Kashima fork, 160 mm of travel
Rear suspension: FOX FLOAT X Factory Kashima shock
Wheels: DT Swiss H1900 SPLINE, in a mixed setup with a 29-inch front wheel and a 27.5-inch rear wheel
Tyres: Schwalbe Albert EVO Trail
Brakes: Shimano DEORE XT four-piston disc brakes
Display: 2.2-inch colour display on the top tube, with a USB-C port for charging a device

An electric-assist mountain bike, or e-MTB, still has pedals. The motor adds power only while the rider pedals, and the battery capacity, measured in watt-hours (Wh), is a rough guide to how long that help can last. The 720 Wh figure is Honda's battery capacity. Honda's pages reviewed here do not state a range, because range depends on the rider, the terrain and the assistance level chosen.

The following is general background from a reference article on electric bicycles, not a statement about the RN0. A bike with pedal assist, often called a pedelec, only helps while the rider pedals. Sensors measure how fast or how hard the rider pedals, or both, and the controller sets the motor output to match. The article says that bikes from the 2020s commonly use torque sensors, which give smoother power delivery.

Electric mountain bikes often put the motor near the pedals, a layout called a mid-drive. Because that motor drives the chain and the bike's own gears, the same article says mid-drive power is usually limited to roughly 250 to 500 W to reduce wear. Honda lists the RN0's maximum output at 750 W, so it quotes a peak figure; it has not said what continuous rating applies.

In the European Union, the standard EN 15194 defines a pedelec as a bike whose motor helps above 6 km/h only while the rider pedals, cuts out at 25 km/h, and has a maximum continuous rated power of 250 W, though it may briefly exceed that. Honda's pages do not say which legal class the RN0 will fall into in any market, and rules in other countries can differ.

The same article notes that range depends on assistance level, battery size, speed, hills and the combined weight of bike and rider, and gives about 40 to 120 km per charge as a typical spread for e-bikes in general. Honda has not published a range for the RN0.

Honda's European press release describes the RN0 as an all-new electric mountain bike and Honda's first entry into the European e-MTB market, and lists it among its key announcements for 2027. It names ROTWILD and Shimano as development partners.
The bike uses a larger 29-inch wheel at the front and a smaller 27.5-inch wheel at the rear. Honda lists the sizes but does not explain its reasons in the pages reviewed here.

Price and sale date
Which countries will sell it, and whether it will come to India
Claimed range
How many bikes will be made
EICMA 2026 runs at Fiera Milano from 3 to 8 November 2026. Press days were 3 and 4 November, and public days are 5 to 8 November.

articles.title: Cabinet Approves Rs 10,000 Crore Container Scheme (Oct 2026)
articles.excerpt: The Union Cabinet approved a Rs 10,000 crore scheme to build shipping containers in India, running to FY 2039-40. The government says it aims for about tenfold capacity.
blocks: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme on 28 October 2026, according to the UNI news agency. The scheme has an outlay of Rs 10,000 crore and runs until the financial year 2039-40. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced the decision after the Cabinet meeting. One other report, from IBEF, gives the approval date as 29 October. The scheme was first announced in the Union Budget for 2026-27. This article is correct as of 4 November 2026.

The government's stated aims are to build a globally competitive container manufacturing industry in India, reduce dependence on imports and strengthen supply chains. It targets raising annual container manufacturing capacity about tenfold, to 7.5 lakh twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs). A TEU is the standard measure of container capacity, equal to one 20-foot container.
What a TEU is and why the target is stated that way

Most shipping containers are 8 feet (2.4 m) wide and either 20 feet or 40 feet long, under the ISO 668 standard. A TEU counts one standard 20-foot container as one unit, so a 40-foot container is two TEU, whatever its height. A reference article on intermodal containers says 40-foot boxes make up about 70 percent of the world's container volume measured in TEU. The scheme's target of 7.5 lakh TEUs a year is therefore a measure of capacity, not a count of boxes.
Why container manufacturing is a policy topic

The same reference article says about 90 percent of the world's containers are made in China. The government's own stated reasons, as reported by UNI and IBEF, are to reduce import dependence and strengthen supply chains. This article does not assess those aims; it only reports them.

A standard container is a closed steel box made of corrugated weathering steel with a plywood floor, with a steel casting at each of its eight corners used for lifting, stacking and securing. IBEF lists specialised steel, corner castings, wooden frames and paints among the industries the scheme is meant to support, which fits that construction.

Operational expenditure assistance: Rs 8,891 crore, for containers made to international shipping standards and sold by eligible manufacturers
Interest subvention: Rs 859 crore, a 3 percent a year subsidy on interest for eligible term loans, for new (greenfield) plants and expansions of existing (brownfield) plants
Testing and certification: Rs 150 crore, including common testing facilities, for example for dynamic longitudinal impact testing
These three amounts add up to Rs 9,900 crore, which is Rs 100 crore less than the stated outlay. The two reports opened for this article do not explain the difference.

The government estimates about 3,000 direct jobs and more than 50,000 indirect jobs. IBEF says the scheme is also meant to support related industries such as specialised steel, corner castings, wooden flooring frames and paints.

A search of official material found a figure reported as Rs 49,500 for a 20-foot container and Rs 86,625 for a 40-foot container under the operational expenditure assistance. The government pages opened for this article did not show these numbers, so they are not confirmed here and should be checked against the official release.

Schemes of this kind are normally put into effect through guidelines issued by the ministry responsible, which set out who can apply and how payments are claimed. The reports opened for this article did not name the ministry or give a date for the guidelines, so readers should not assume a start date from the Cabinet approval alone. The scheme's long run, to the financial year 2039-40, means that payments are planned over about 13 years.
What the reports do not say

Detailed eligibility conditions, which the pages opened for this article do not set out
When applications open
Which companies or locations may take part

The Cabinet decision is a government approval of a scheme. How it works in practice depends on the guidelines the responsible ministry issues. Readers who need exact conditions should consult the official release and the scheme guidelines.
